# M0-d-07 — the closing check's notes (not failing lines)

These notes come from the closing check of item M0-d-07 (lane `check/M0-d-07-close-r3`, 2026-10-03). Under the
session's ruling J162, the closing check fails the item only on a blocker. Every finding below is a contrived or
deliberate writer's escape, a hardening test, or a claim to tighten, so none of them fails the item. Each row names
its handling and the milestone where it belongs. The verdict and its evidence are in `checks/M0-d-07.md` (round r3).

| id | observation | suggested handling | milestone |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | flatbush 4.6.2's `this.nodeSize ** level` (`index.js:300`, `flatbush.js:341`) is still an open reviewed exception (C-0126). `vendor/patches/` holds only the delaunator and simplex-noise patches, and no routing line has followed round 0's. CONFIRMED by grep. | Route an exact-multiplication patch through M0-s-01's files (`vendor/patches/`). §6.5 (4) says "patched or wrapped … before adoption". | M0, before M0-a-03 writes `kernel/src/adapters/flatbush.ts` in wave 4 (PLAUSIBLE timing) |
| N2 | A second ESLint configuration placed in a folder that `walkTree` skips escapes model-coverage. Examples of such folders: any `coverage/`, `packages/<pkg>/dist/`, `bench/dist/`. CONFIRMED in a scratch copy. `packages/kernel/zz/coverage/eslint.config.mjs` exported `[{ files: ['**/*.{js,mjs}'], plugins: { plat }, rules: { ...MODEL_RULES } }]`, and `packages/kernel/zz/coverage/n.mjs` held `Math.sin(1) + 2 ** 0.5`, re-exported by a kernel source. For n.mjs, `isPathIgnored` was false and the computed configuration carried the whole model rule set, so the check counted the file as linted. But ESLint's directory walk never enters `coverage/` (plat/'s ignores), so the file was never linted, and `node scripts/lint.mjs` exited 0. A deliberate writer's escape: C-0130 (1)'s "refuses every ESLint configuration file in plat/ but the root's" is narrowed by the walk's skips. | Make model-coverage require each closure file to be among the files the tree lint actually linted. Two ways: pass `scripts/lint.mjs`'s results to the check, or lint the closure list itself. Another way is to search for configuration files without the walk's skips. | M4 |
| N3 | The check's `config === undefined` branch after a false `isPathIgnored` has no test: mutant MC10 (`[]` for an undefined configuration) survives with `Tests 118 passed (118)`. In ESLint 10.12 the branch is unreachable. A probe ran a `.ts` file under a nested `export default [{}]`: `isPathIgnored` gave true and `calculateConfigForFile` gave undefined. So such a file is refused as ignored, and the check fails closed. But the message then says "eslint.config.js ignores it" for a file that no configuration matches. | Add one case with a stub ESLint that returns undefined, and word the message "ignored, or matched by no configuration". | M4 |
| N4 | Round r2's N2 is unchanged, and the disagreement it describes now involves two checks. The adapter's `../../node_modules/flatbush/index.js` spelling is allowed by dependency-direction (C-0129 (3)). But it fails closed in both inline-directives and model-coverage, as C-0130 (1) states. Safe, but the parts disagree. | When the closure walk is next touched (the blocker B1's fix touches it), treat a path into `node_modules` as the package it names, as dependency-direction does. | M4, or with B1's fix |
| N5 | Round r1's N3 – N5 escapes are unchanged. Re-planted in one kernel source, these pass with lint exit 0 (CONFIRMED): `({}).constructor.keys({ b: 1 })`, `eval('Math.sin(1)')`, `[3, 1].sort(void 0)` and `new WeakRef({})`. Not re-planted this round: `spawnSync('sh', ['-c', 'pnpm test'])` and fs path literals. These are deliberate writers' escapes, or forms outside C-0093's and C-0127 (2)'s letter. | Refuse `constructor` member reads of key-enumeration methods, `eval` / `Function`, a `sort` argument that is not a function, and `WeakRef` / `FinalizationRegistry` in model code. Extend no-bare-pnpm to shell `-c` strings. | M4 |
| N6 | Added by the closing check r4 (lane `check/M0-d-07-close-r4`). A code file that the vendored scan does not read (`.jsx` or `.tsx`; the scan reads `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.mts` and `.cts`) placed in a vendored library's folder, and reached through the node_modules spelling, passes the lint. CONFIRMED in a scratch copy: `vendor/flatbush@4.6.2/zz.jsx` held `Math.sin(1) + 2 ** 0.5`, and `packages/kernel/src/adapters/flatbush.ts` re-exported it from `../../node_modules/flatbush/zz.jsx`. `node scripts/lint.mjs` exited 0 (`vendor-scan ok`, `model-coverage ok`), because `digestClosure` lists it in `vendored`. The bare name `flatbush/zz.jsx` reaches the same file through the older path. This narrows C-0131 (2)'s claim that the lint "never accepts, for a vendored library, bytes the scan did not read". `corepack pnpm vendor:verify` refuses the file (`flatbush@4.6.2/zz.jsx: not in the lock`, exit 1), so only a writer who also rewrites the lock gets through. A deliberate writer's escape. | Make the vendored branch (and the bare-name branch) require `isScannedFile` for a reached code file, or widen the scan's `CODE` to every code extension (C-0128's list). Then word C-0131 (2)'s claim "with vendor:verify". | M4 |
